record.title: MorFiC reports critic-conditioned transfer across quadruped morphologies
record.summary: The March 15 preprint presents MorFiC, which conditions a shared policy's critic on robot morphology using feature-wise modulation. The authors report improved zero-shot quadruped transfer after simulation training with morphology randomization, including speed gains of 16.1% on A1, about 2× on Cheetah and about 5× on B1 versus morphology-conditioned PPO baselines. They also report deployment on Unitree Go1 and Go2 without fine-tuning. The paper reports these results; this review did not inspect the full evaluation tables, physical-robot protocol, code or independent reproductions.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that MorFiC, a morphology-conditioned critic using feature-wise modulation in a shared actor-critic policy, improves zero-shot quadruped transfer after simulation training with morphology randomization. The abstract reports speed gains of 16.1% on A1, about 2× on Cheetah and about 5× on B1 relative to morphology-conditioned PPO baselines, plus deployment on Go1 and Go2 robots without fine-tuning. These are paper-reported results, not independent measurements in this review.

evidence_gaps.description: The abstract gives selected speed gains and says the policy was deployed on two Unitree platforms without fine-tuning, but this review did not inspect task counts, robot test conditions, failure rates, uncertainty, or a replication.

brief.importance_rationale: If the paper's results hold, critic-side morphology conditioning could reduce value-estimation interference and improve policy transfer across quadruped bodies, affecting a meaningful robotics training choice. Its importance is bounded to locomotion and the small set of reported platforms; it does not establish general robot transfer.
limitations: All quantitative performance results are author-reported in a preprint and were not independently reproduced here.
The headline simulation velocity gains do not show task-level success, safety, robustness or economic performance across robot platforms.
The physical deployment claim is limited in the abstract to Unitree Go1 and Go2 without fine-tuning; the test conditions and failure rates were not inspected.
The result concerns quadruped locomotion and does not establish general morphology transfer to other robot types.

The authors report improved zero-shot quadruped transfer after simulation training with morphology randomization, including speed gains of 16.1% on A1, about 2× on Cheetah and about 5× on B1 versus morphology-conditioned PPO baselines. technical.claimed_result: The paper reports zero-shot quadruped speed gains of 16.1% on A1, approximately 2× on Cheetah and approximately 5× on B1, plus no-fine-tuning deployment on Unitree Go1 and Go2.
technical.compute_or_cost: No compute budget, energy, training cost or per-task operating cost was recovered from the abstract.
technical.demonstrated_result: No result independently demonstrated in this activation; the reported results are claims in the primary preprint.
technical.implementation_status: The preprint describes shared actor-critic training with morphology-aware FiLM modulation of critic features; public implementation availability was not checked.
technical.mechanism: A morphology encoder supplies latent robot parameters to FiLM layers in the critic, so the value function can vary across embodiments while the policy remains shared.
technical.novelty: The paper argues that critic-side morphology conditioning reduces value-target interference and stabilizes advantages under morphology variation.
technical.regime: Quadruped locomotion; training uses one source robot with morphology randomization in simulation, followed by evaluations on other simulated morphologies and two Unitree robot platforms according to the abstract.
technical.reproducibility: Primary abstract and university summary are accessible; full tables, physical test conditions, code and independent reproduction were not inspected.
technical.strongest_baseline: The abstract names morphology-conditioned PPO baselines; exact configurations and per-robot comparisons require full-paper inspection.

brief.title: MorFiC reports critic-conditioned transfer across quadruped morphologies
brief.why_it_matters: Robots with different body dynamics can invalidate a shared policy's value estimates. If the reported results hold, morphology-conditioned critic features may offer a practical way to transfer locomotion policies without retraining each robot. Current evidence is limited to the authors' stated quadruped simulations and two Unitree deployments, and does not establish safe general-purpose transfer.
